newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT - Australia 10-yr bond revving up for 93.015.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Australia 10-yr bond revving up for 93.015.

text.p: *The Australian 10-year bond futures contract is in sight of the 93.015 peak set last December following Thursday's strong advance on a weak labour force report.
*September bills are all but pricing in a 50 basis point interest rate cut at a SYCOM close of 94.91, or 5.09 percent.
The June Australian 10-year bond futures contract is in sight of the 93.015 peak set last December after extending Thursday's strong advance in SYCOM on the prospect of a further policy easing.
The contract ended after hours trading at 92.955, up from Thursday's 92.880 close and after touching a high of 92.970.
A break of the December high would take the market to levels not seen since February 1994 and will see the equivalent 10-year yield go below 7.0 percent.
Such a move would see the contract targetting 93.180, analysts said.
The chances of an easing in official 5.5 percent cash rates was seen as a strong possibility, even as early as this morning, following Thursday's extremely weak labour force report for May.
The September bill futures contract is all but pricing in a 50 basis point rate cut at a SYCOM close of 94.91, which equates to a cash rate of 5.09 percent.

The market will be holding a collective breath at 9.30 a.m. (2330 GMT) when the Reserve Bank usually announces policy changes amid the feeling that if the central bank remains concerned over rising unemployment and still desires growth there is little reason to wait for July 1 board meeting.

Even the RBA's possible concern of easing in the face of the Federal Reserve tightening policy at next month's FOMC meeting would have lessened after U.S. retail sales dropped for the third consecutive month in May, analysts said.
The last time sales dropped three months in a row was during September to November 1981. The May data fell 0.1 percent when a 0.3 percent rise had been expected.

U.S. Treasuries rallied on the data amid the view that U.S. growth is slowing to a more sustainable level after the rapid expansion in the fourth quarter last year and the first quarter of 1997. --Colin Brinsden 61-2 9373-1800
